newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Newly privatised Tunis stock exchange reports profits.
newsitem.headline: Newly privatised Tunis stock exchange reports profits.

text.p: The Tunis stock exchange on Friday reported profits twice its capital during 1996, its first year of private management.
Mohamed Hadouej, chairman of the Bourse des Valeurs Mobilieres de Tunis (BVMT) announced that pre-tax profits amounted to 1.1 million dinars.
"It is almost double...the capital," he told the BVMT's annual general meeting, its first since it was privatised in November 1995.
The stock exchange is now run by traders through BVMT and a separate watchdog group called the Financial Market Council.

"The most important fact in 1996 was that we introduced the new computerised dealing system which was an important step toward the international standards of the stock markets," Hadouej told the meeting.

The system was set up with the help of the Paris Bourse. Firms listed had been progressively introduced since October 1996 on the computerised dealing system which is now at 26 out of thirty-two companies listed.
The system was installed in the new headquarters where BVMT has moved last year in a Tunis business center.

Hadouej said that a fund to garrantee the market's risks was set up by BVMT during the last three months and has now assets amounting to 500,000 dinars. The fund aims at paying amounts a broker would fail to honor.
BVMT earns 10 percent of revenues from the fund's assets it invests, mainly on the bonds market, he said.
"These actions and results were done despite a difficult bourse situation in which the volume of exchanges dropped by around 30 percent in 1996 compared to 1995," he added.
In 1996, the capital market turnover shrunk 33 percent to 625 million dinars from a record 927 million dinars in 1995. The index lost 10 percent in a year, reaching 570.643 points at the end of 1996.

Brokers said that the slump was because most of the computerised shares dropped sharply when they made the switch and because of the new rules implemented to introduce more transparency to the market.
The index continued to drop in January and February 1997, and has started a slow recovery in March. It closed at 499.65 on Friday. ($=1.09 dinar)
